correctness.summary: For a minimal MEB contact certificate, the weighted pairwise variance identity gives R^2 exactly. Adding and subtracting D^2 times the pair-weight sum yields the three nonnegative deficit terms. The support thresholds, weight estimates, edge bounds, and volume consequence follow by direct inequalities from that identity.

limitations: The estimates control the active MEB contact simplex, not all points of the original compact set.
The support-cardinality thresholds are sharp, but the per-edge and volume constants are not claimed optimal.
The Rips-Cech interpretation is simplexwise and is not a new global persistence-stability theorem.
Originality is to the best of our knowledge; the elementary identity may have an equivalent formulation under different terminology.

originality.scope: to the best of our knowledge
originality.summary: Classical Jung theory, MEB support-set characterizations, isodiametric variance bounds, finite Jung constants, simplex stability, and Rips-Cech comparisons were checked. No located source states the exact cardinality/weight/edge Jung-deficit decomposition together with the derived sharp support thresholds and quantitative active-simplex regularity.

review_statement: Same-model review: passed. Independent audit: not yet performed.

value.summary: The identity refines Jung's scalar extremal bound into a structural certificate, separating three independent sources of slack and yielding sharp support-cardinality phase transitions plus quantitative near-regularity of the active simplex.
